senses.gloss: f. (פתר to extend, cmp. Assyr. paššaru dish, v. Fränkel, Lexicogr. p. 53) table.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 25:23">Targ. Ex. XXV, 23</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 9:2">Targ. Prov. IX, 2</cite> <he>פתורת׳</he>.—
Targ. Y. Gen. XXIII, 16 פָּתוֹר (ed. Vien. פְּ׳) money-changer’s table.—
Sabb. 36ᵃ פתורה פתורתא פתורתא פתורה what formerly was called pathora (a small table, plate) is now called pathorta, and vice versa.
<cite ref="Taanit 25a">Taan. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>פ׳ דדהבא</he> (Ms. M. <he>תכא</he>) a golden table.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 19b:19">B. Kam. 19ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>בבהמה ופ׳</he> it means a domestic animal eating from the table, v. <cite ref="Q02175"><he>פְּתִיתָה</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>פָּתוֹרִין</he>, <he>פָּתוֹרַיָּא</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 21:5">Targ. Is. XXI, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 40:43">Targ. Ez. XL, 43</cite>; a. e.—
Nidd. 20ᵃ הא בפָתוֹרֵי (some ed. sing.) ‘dark clothes coming from abroad’ refers to those worn at the table (vestes cenatoriae or synthesis), v. אוֹלָרִין.
